ADDL MACT UDUPIPARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The present appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 22.03.2012 in MVC.No.157/2009 passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Udupi, for seeking enhancement of compensation.
2. The factum of accident is not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments from both sides and perused the records.
4.
The Tribunal has awarded global compensation of Rs.20,000/- along with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

5. From the evidence on record, it is proved that the claimant had sustained the following injuries:
i. 2x1cm laceration (2x1x1cm over lateral end of right supra orbital ridge; ii. 2x1x0.5 laceration over left frontal skull 3 compensation above lateral end of left supra-orbital ridge.
Praveen vs Rajan Shetty on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181118104/
2 6.

The doctor - P.W.2 is examined before the Tribunal and he has stated that the claimant had suffered permanent disability at 9% towards left upper limb function and 7% towards right upper limb function.
The claimant is an electrician by profession in Aluminium Fabrication Industry at the time of the accident.
Therefore, certainly, the accidental injuries and disability sustained affects the earning capacity of the claimant.

Therefore, considering the nature of injuries sustained and evidence of the doctor-P.W.2 and upon following the principle of law laid by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another 1, it is just and proper to take functional disability at 7% towards the whole body and this causes loss of earning capacity due to disability.

Accordingly, compensation of Rs.68,040/- is awarded under the head loss of earning capacity due to disability.
8. Further compensation of Rs.25,000/- is awarded under the head injury, pain and suffering.
9. The claimant was admitted in the hospital for a period of 5 days.
Hence, compensation of Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head medical expenses and hospitalization charges.
10. Further compensation of Rs.9,000/- (Rs.4,500/- p.m., x 2 months) is awarded under the head loss of income during laid up period considering for a period of two months.
11. Further compensation of Rs.15,000/- is awarded under the head loss of amenities.

14 . The Tribunal has awarded global compensation of Rs.20,000/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,47,040/-.
Hence, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,27,040/- (Rs.1,47,040/- - Rs.20,000/-).
Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,27,040/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

15. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 22.03.2012 in MVC.No.157/2009 passed by the Prl. Senior Civil Judge and Addl. MACT, Udupi, is modified to the extent that the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,27,040/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iii.
No order as to costs.
iv. The appellant/claimant is not entitled for interest for the delay period of 19 days in filing the appeal.
v. Registry is directed to transmit the TCR along with copy of this order to the Tribunal forthwith.

vi.
Draw award accordingly.
